descripcion_geo: The longest river in the world (6,650 km), fertilizes the narrow strip of Egypt. Its annual floods made Egyptian civilization possible.
importancia_estrategica: Backbone of Egyptian civilization; scene of the exodus and childhood of Moses.

historias.titulo: The baby Moses in the Nile
historias.descripcion: Moses's mother puts him in a papyrus basket in the Nile to save him from the decree of death; The pharaoh's daughter finds him and adopts him.

historias.titulo: The first plague: the Nile turns to blood
historias.descripcion: Moses strikes the Nile with his staff and the water turns to blood; all the fish die.

historias.titulo: Joseph and the dream of the Nile
historias.descripcion: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows and seven thin ones coming out of the Nile; Joseph interprets it as seven years of plenty and seven of famine.

personajes.descripcion: Saved from the waters of the Nile as a baby; Then he turned those waters into blood as a sign before Pharaoh.
His interpretation of the Nile dream brought him to power in Egypt and saved two nations from famine.
He rescued the baby Moses from the Nile and adopted him as his son.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The Nile was divinity in Egypt (Hapi); His conversion into blood was a direct blow to the heart of Egyptian religiosity.

judaismo.descripcion: The first plague turned the sacred Nile into blood, declaring that the God of Israel surpasses the Egyptian river-god.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The first plague turned the sacred Nile into blood, declaring that the God of Israel surpasses the Egyptian river-god.

cristianismo.descripcion: The baby Moses saved from the waters is seen as a prefiguration of Jesus saved from Herod's slaughter (Mt 2:13-16).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The baby Moses saved from the waters is seen as a prefiguration of Jesus saved from Herod's slaughter (Mt 2:13-16).

islam.descripcion: Musa (Moses) appears in the Quran; His story on the Nile is told in Cor 20:37-40.
islam.significado_teologico: Musa (Moses) appears in the Quran; His story on the Nile is told in Cor 20:37-40.
